description: We are a team of curious CSE students passionate about AI, data analysis, and software development. We aim to use technology to explore space and Earth science and solve real-world problems. We welcome creative, enthusiastic teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, UI/UX, web development, GIS, or research. Beginners eager to learn are welcome too! Let's collaborate, innovate, and build something impactful at NASA Space Apps!
summary:
VYOMA – Astronaut Health Intelligence System is an intelligent health monitoring and self-management platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It addresses health challenges associated with microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and changing space environments by integrating physiological, behavioral, and environmental health monitoring.

VYOMA enables astronauts to track vital signs, sleep patterns, stress levels, and environmental conditions through a unified dashboard. Its personalized health analysis engine compares current measurements against individual health baselines to identify unusual patterns and potential risks. An AI-powered health assistant helps astronauts understand health changes, interpret alerts, and access actionable, protocol-based guidance. The platform also emphasizes offline accessibility, ensuring essential health records and monitoring capabilities remain available during communication disruptions.

By combining personalized health insights, anomaly detection, and intelligent decision support, VYOMA aims to empower astronauts to take a more proactive role in managing their health and well-being throughout space missions.
details:
VYOMA – Space Health Intelligence System

Space missions can last for months or even years, and keeping astronauts healthy throughout these missions is a major challenge. VYOMA is our attempt to address this challenge through a digital platform that helps monitor astronaut health, identify unusual changes in vital signs and provide useful health insights in one place.

How VYOMA works

The platform is built around four main modules:

  1. Dashboard: Gives a quick overview of an astronaut's health, including recent readings, overall status and important alerts.
  2. VitalWatch: Keeps track of important health parameters such as heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, body temperature and respiratory rate. It also allows users to view historical readings and compare them with individual baselines.
  3. HealthSense AI: Examines changes in physiological readings and highlights values that differ from an astronaut's usual baseline. It also provides explanations and suggested checks to help users understand these changes.
  4. Alerts & Triage: Brings abnormal readings to the user's attention, displays their severity and allows alerts to be acknowledged and resolved.

NASA resources and how we used them

While developing VYOMA, we referred to NASA's Human Research Program resource, 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight. It helped us understand some of the major health challenges astronauts may face during space missions and guided our thinking while designing the platform.

We considered the five hazards in the following ways:

  • Radiation: Helped us recognize the importance of considering radiation exposure when thinking about astronaut health and environmental safety.
  • Isolation and confinement: Made us consider the psychological well-being of astronauts and the need for support during long missions.
  • Distance from Earth: Highlighted why reliable health monitoring is important when astronauts may not have immediate access to medical support from Earth.
  • Gravity fields: Helped us understand why physiological changes associated with spaceflight should be considered when monitoring vital signs.
  • Hostile and closed environments: Encouraged us to consider how environmental conditions inside a spacecraft could affect astronaut health.

We used this NASA resource as a reference while planning the project; it is not directly connected to the application's data system. The current prototype uses simulated astronaut telemetry for demonstration and testing. It does not use actual astronaut medical records or live NASA spacecraft data.

Technologies and tools used

We developed the backend using Python and FastAPI, with PostgreSQL to store astronaut profiles, vital readings and health alerts. SQLAlchemy handles database interactions, while Pydantic is used for data validation and API schemas. The frontend brings these components together through dashboards, charts and interactive monitoring screens.

We also used AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude during development. They helped us with debugging, understanding technical concepts, improving code and refining the user interface. OpenAI's image-generation tools were used to create some of the illustrations included in the website. These images are clearly marked as AI-generated.

Expected impact

Through VYOMA, we aim to demonstrate how a single platform can make astronaut health information easier to monitor and understand. By bringing together vital readings, historical trends, explainable insights and alerts, the system could help medical teams identify unusual changes and review them more efficiently during long-duration missions.

VYOMA is currently a prototype developed for demonstration and research purposes. Its simulated readings, thresholds and automated insights have not been clinically validated. The platform is intended to support health monitoring concepts, not replace professional medical judgement.
